title: Poppy and the Pebble Elf
markdown:
The sun, like a giant golden buttercup, peeked over the leafy canopy of Whispering Woods. It painted dappled patterns across the mossy ground, as if a sprite had been playing with a paintbrush. The oaks rustled. The forest hummed itself awake.

Poppy the hedgehog, a creature of speedy scurries and determined little legs, was on a very important mission. Her quills, usually neat, quivered with urgency. She was off to visit her dear friend Cerys the badger, whose berry tarts were legendary: plump juicy berries baked into warm crumbly goodness. Poppy simply had to get there before they were all gobbled up.

She scampered along the well-worn path, legs a blur, past ferns that tickled her nose and a patch of wild strawberries she did not even stop to count. “Faster, faster,” she whispered to her twitching whiskers. Her heart beat a quick cheerful rhythm, a tiny drummer. Ahead, the Glimmering Stream winked, a silver ribbon in the sunlight. Usually it was a friendly helper, with a neat row of perfectly placed mossy stepping-stones for all its visitors. Today, when Poppy reached its bubbly edge, her small nose twitched with a puzzled sniff. The stones were gone. Vanished as if by a trick. All that was left was wide swirling sparkly water, looking awfully deep and very un-crossable. A water-skater dimpled the surface and skated on, which did not help a hedgehog in the least.

The moss seemed to quiver with her frustration. She stamped a little hedgehog foot. “Oh, bother and brambles.” She tried a brave leap, but the stream was much too wide. Her quills bristled like a prickly question mark. She was stuck, and the thought of Cerys’s empty tart plate made her sigh a big gusty sigh.

Down by the stream, nestled among smooth grey pebbles that gleamed like polished eggs, lived a very shy pebble elf named Glint. His eyes sparkled like tiny bits of amber. His wings looked woven from cobwebs and moonlight. He loved to watch the world unfold, and he had often seen Poppy’s speedy scurries.

Peeking from behind a particularly round comfortable pebble, Glint saw Poppy’s sad stuck face. He knew a little secret about the Glimmering Stream, a secret his pebble folk shared in hushed whispers. Talking to hedgehogs, especially speedy busy ones when they were feeling huffy, made his tiny elf heart flutter like a trapped butterfly. He could not just watch her be sad. With a deep shaky breath, he fluttered out.

“Hullo,” Glint whispered, soft as silver bells.

Poppy, still grumbling, did not quite look up. “Can’t you see I’m in a bit of a muddle? The stepping-stones have all disappeared. And I’m going to miss all the delicious berry tarts.”

At her cross words, Glint’s delicate wings drooped. “Oh,” he said softly, and with a quiet almost silent sigh he zipped back to the cozy safety of his pebble friends. The stream seemed to chuckle, bubbling a bit faster, as if sharing a private joke. Poppy’s face fell. She had not meant to sound so cross, not really, but the thought of those tarts…

Glint nestled into his pebble, a little sad and a little misunderstood. As he sat, listening to the stream’s murmuring song, a memory surfaced, clear as a raindrop. His grandmother, another wise pebble elf, had shared her wisdom on a bright sunshiny day. “Kindness, Glint,” she had said, voice as soft as a summer breeze on a flower, “is the strongest magic there is. It can make things appear that were never seen before, and it can mend what seems broken.”

Poppy, now quite worried and a little lonely, watched him disappear. She had been so busy thinking about her problem she had hardly noticed the little elf at all. The sun, so bright a moment before, tiptoed behind a fluffy grey cloud. The stream gurgled and swirled, almost impatient. She thought of sweet juicy red berries and warm crumbly tarts, and then of how very alone she felt on the bank.

She took a deep breath that puffed her hedgehog cheeks, stood as tall as she could, and brushed a speck of dusty leaf off her nose. She looked toward the pebble cluster. “Glint?” This time her voice was softer, not a dry twig snapping, more like an autumn leaf falling. “Glint, please. Do you know any magic that could help me cross the stream? I would be ever so, ever so grateful if you did.”

As her kind gentle words floated on the air, a soft shimmery light bloomed from the water itself. First one, then another, then a whole row of smooth mossy stepping-stones began to rise from the Glimmering Stream, as if painted there by moonlight. They were perfectly spaced, just right for a hedgehog’s quick feet.

Glint peeked out, saw the stones, saw Poppy’s astonished happy face light up like a firefly, and fluttered forth, amber eyes shining.

Poppy looked at Glint, then at the shimmering stones, and a warm feeling spread through her, much nicer than any rushing. “Oh, Glint. You knew. Thank you, thank you so much.”

Glint beamed, shyness melting like frost in morning sun. “It was your kind words, Poppy,” he whispered, voice now clear and strong.

Poppy smiled a wide genuine hedgehog smile, fizzy as lemonade. “Let’s cross together.”

Side by side, the quick-footed hedgehog and the tiny pebble elf walked the sparkling stones, their shadows dancing on the water. Beyond the far bank, the path to Cerys’s burrow waited, and the tarts, still warm, would taste even better shared after a crossing earned by a gentler voice.
